### STEP 1 — Scene
A mixed meal of cheese-and-tomato pizza pieces, leafy salad with olives, a little penne pasta, broccoli, and cherry tomatoes.

### STEP 2 — Vessel
A large, rounded-square dinner plate, approximately 27 cm across. Using a circular approximation:
**Area = 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 572 cm².**

### STEPS 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
Area percentages below represent separate food footprints; dressing overlaps the salad.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Density → weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cheese-and-tomato pizza pieces | 30% | 172 × 1.3 = 224 ml | 0.9 → 201 g | 270 | 543 kcal |
| Mixed leafy greens, including leaves near pasta | 22% | 126 × 2.5 = 315 ml | 0.15 → 47 g | 20 | 9 kcal |
| Cooked penne pasta | 6% | 34 × 1.5 = 51 ml | 0.8 → 41 g | 155 | 64 kcal |
| Broccoli | 7% | 40 × 2.5 = 100 ml | 0.55 → 55 g | 35 | 19 kcal |
| Cherry tomatoes | 6% | 34 × 2 = 68 ml | 0.65 → 44 g | 20 | 9 kcal |
| Black olives | 1% | 6 × 1.5 = 9 ml | 0.65 → 6 g | 145 | 9 kcal |
| Visible oily dressing/coating | Overlapping | Approximately 6 ml | Approximately 1 → 6 g | 880 | 53 kcal |

### STEP 8 — Sanity check
The food footprints total **72%** of the plate, consistent with the visible empty space. The small pasta portion and olives receive small weights, while the pizza provides most of the energy.

**Estimated total: 400 g and 705 kcal.** The main uncertainty is the pizza’s thickness and the amount of oil.
